candidates.hypothesis: Deterministic intervention: retain only the first record for each normalized-content hash. The frozen within-arm comparator preserves all records and is otherwise identical, including fields, labels, order, passage sizing, normalization, and aggregation. For BM25, content-hash-first handling is prospectively expected to produce higher recall_at_100/out by preventing exact duplicates from perturbing corpus statistics or occupying multiple result positions. The hypothesis is falsified if candidate recall_at_100/out minus comparator recall_at_100/out is less than or equal to zero. This is a diagnostic, non-advancing ARM-01 test.

Deterministic intervention: append claims_text after title and abstract. The frozen within-arm comparator uses only title and abstract in that order, with every other program setting identical. For BM25, the candidate is prospectively expected to produce higher recall_at_100/out because claim language may expose additional exact lexical matches. The hypothesis is falsified if candidate recall_at_100/out minus comparator recall_at_100/out is less than or equal to zero. This is a diagnostic, non-advancing ARM-01 test.

Deterministic intervention: replace the literal labels "title: ", "abstract: ", and "claims: " with empty strings. The frozen within-arm comparator uses those three literal labels and is otherwise identical, including field selection, order, passage sizing, normalization, duplicate handling, and aggregation. For BM25, the unlabeled candidate is prospectively expected to produce higher recall_at_100/out by avoiding repeated structural tokens in document statistics. The hypothesis is falsified if candidate recall_at_100/out minus comparator recall_at_100/out is less than or equal to zero. This is a diagnostic, non-advancing ARM-01 test.

Deterministic intervention: reduce logical passage size from 768 tokens to 384 tokens while retaining a 64-token overlap. The frozen within-arm comparator uses 768-token passages with 64-token overlap and is otherwise identical. For BM25 with max-passage family aggregation, the 384-token candidate is prospectively expected to produce higher recall_at_100/out through more localized term-frequency and length-normalization signals. The hypothesis is falsified if candidate recall_at_100/out minus comparator recall_at_100/out is less than or equal to zero. This is a diagnostic, non-advancing ARM-01 test.

For lexical/bm25s, the sole deterministic intervention is replacing family-level units with fixed 512-token passages having 64-token overlap, a conservative size under the 4096-token arm limit. Against the frozen within-arm comparator using family units with identical fields, order, empty labels, normalization, duplicate policy, and avg_top3 family aggregation, recall_at_100/out is expected to be higher; the hypothesis is falsified if it is less than or equal to the comparator. This ARM-01 candidate is diagnostic and non-advancing.

For lexical/bm25s, the sole deterministic intervention is adding claims_text to title and abstract. Against the frozen within-arm comparator using only title and abstract with identical order, empty labels, family unitization, normalization, duplicate policy, and aggregation, recall_at_100/out is expected to be higher; the hypothesis is falsified if it is less than or equal to the comparator. This ARM-01 candidate is diagnostic and non-advancing.

For lexical/bm25s, the sole deterministic intervention is removing claims_text while retaining title and abstract. Against the frozen within-arm comparator using title, abstract, and claims_text with identical order, empty labels, family unitization, normalization, duplicate policy, and aggregation, recall_at_100/out is expected to be lower; the hypothesis is falsified if it is greater than or equal to the comparator. This ARM-01 candidate is diagnostic and non-advancing.

For lexical/bm25s, the sole deterministic intervention is changing normalization from unicode_nfkc_whitespace to unicode_nfkc_whitespace_lower. Against the frozen within-arm comparator with case-preserving unicode_nfkc_whitespace and otherwise identical fields, order, empty labels, family unitization, duplicate policy, and aggregation, recall_at_100/out is expected to be higher; the hypothesis is falsified if it is less than or equal to the comparator. This ARM-01 candidate is diagnostic and non-advancing.

For BAAI/bge-m3 dense retrieval with the frozen 8192-token arm limit, deterministically preserving every duplicate representation is the sole intervention relative to the frozen within-arm comparator, which uses the same labeled title, abstract, and claims_text order, family unitization, case-preserving Unicode NFKC plus whitespace normalization, content-hash-first duplicate handling, and single-unit aggregation. The expected later-test direction is lower recall_at_100/out because redundant dense candidates may occupy retrieval capacity; the hypothesis is falsified if recall_at_100/out is equal to or higher than the comparator. This ARM-02 candidate is diagnostic and non-advancing.

For BAAI/bge-m3 dense retrieval with the frozen 8192-token arm limit, deterministically excluding claims_text while retaining labeled title and abstract is the sole intervention relative to the frozen within-arm comparator, which uses labeled title, abstract, and claims_text in that order, family unitization, case-preserving Unicode NFKC plus whitespace normalization, content-hash-first duplicate handling, and single-unit aggregation. The expected later-test direction is higher recall_at_100/out; the hypothesis is falsified if recall_at_100/out is equal to or lower than the comparator. This ARM-02 candidate is diagnostic and non-advancing.

For BAAI/bge-m3 dense retrieval with the frozen 8192-token arm limit, deterministically selecting claims_text alone is the sole intervention relative to the frozen within-arm comparator, which uses labeled title, abstract, and claims_text in that order, family unitization, case-preserving Unicode NFKC plus whitespace normalization, content-hash-first duplicate handling, and single-unit aggregation. As a matched field-selection ablation, the expected later-test direction is lower recall_at_100/out; the hypothesis is falsified if recall_at_100/out is equal to or higher than the comparator. This ARM-02 candidate is diagnostic and non-advancing.

For BAAI/bge-m3 dense retrieval with the frozen 8192-token arm limit, applying Unicode NFKC plus whitespace normalization followed by deterministic lowercasing is the sole intervention relative to the frozen within-arm comparator, which uses the same labeled title, abstract, and claims_text order, family unitization, case-preserving Unicode NFKC plus whitespace normalization, content-hash-first duplicate handling, and single-unit aggregation. The expected later-test direction is lower recall_at_100/out because casing cues are removed; the hypothesis is falsified if recall_at_100/out is equal to or higher than the comparator. This ARM-02 candidate is diagnostic and non-advancing.

For BAAI/bge-m3 dense retrieval, deterministically retaining only the first occurrence of each normalized content hash is expected to yield higher recall_at_100/out than the frozen comparator that preserves all occurrences, while holding title–abstract–claims_text order, labels, 512-token passages, normalization, and maxp aggregation fixed. The hypothesis is falsified if the content-hash-first candidate does not score strictly higher than that comparator. This ARM-02 test is diagnostic and non-advancing.

For BAAI/bge-m3 dense retrieval, deterministically changing only unitization from frozen 1024-model-token passages with 128-token overlap to 512-model-token passages with 64-token overlap, while holding title–abstract–claims_text order, labels, normalization, duplicate policy, and maxp aggregation fixed, is expected to yield higher recall_at_100/out. The hypothesis is falsified if the candidate does not score strictly higher than that comparator. This ARM-02 test is diagnostic and non-advancing.

For BAAI/bge-m3 dense retrieval, deterministically omitting claims_text while retaining title then abstract is expected to yield lower recall_at_100/out than the frozen comparator that uses title, abstract, and claims_text in that order, with identical labels, 512-token passage unitization, normalization, duplicate policy, and maxp aggregation. The hypothesis is falsified if the omission candidate scores equal to or higher than that comparator. This ARM-02 ablation is diagnostic and non-advancing.

For BAAI/bge-m3 dense retrieval, deterministically applying Unicode NFKC, whitespace normalization, and lowercasing is expected to yield lower recall_at_100/out than the frozen comparator applying Unicode NFKC and whitespace normalization without lowercasing, with all three fields, their order and labels, 512-token passages, duplicate preservation, and maxp aggregation held fixed. The hypothesis is falsified if the lowercased candidate scores equal to or higher than that comparator. This ARM-02 test is diagnostic and non-advancing.

Deterministically aggregate a family with n scored passages by the arithmetic mean of its highest min(3, n) passage scores; a family with n=0 emits no aggregate score and cannot enter retrieval, compared with the frozen within-arm comparator using the maximum passage score with the same n=0 behavior and otherwise identical settings. The falsifiable expectation is higher later recall_at_100/out; failure is recall_at_100/out less than or equal to the comparator.

Deterministically add claims_text after title and abstract, compared with the frozen within-arm comparator selecting only title and abstract in that order while retaining every other program setting.
